title: Sabha: Indraprastha
hook: a message from a dead father: Pandu, through Narada, asks his son to perform the Rajasuya

segments.voice: Yesterday: the halls of the gods, each known by who sits there. Your line was here is what the sky looks like.

Yudhishthira has been listening closely, and he's noticed something. In Indra's hall, among all the sages and gods, Narada named only one human king: Harishchandra. Not the great kings of Yudhishthira's own line, not the heroes of the old stories. One name. Why him? the king asks. And there's a second question underneath. In Yama's hall, among the dead, you saw my father. You saw Pandu. What did he say?
screen: `ONE KING IN INDRA'S HALL.` → `WHY HARISHCHANDRA?` → `AND MY FATHER?`

segments.voice: Narada answers the first question first. Harishchandra was a mighty king who brought other kings under him and then performed the great sacrifice called the Rajasuya. He gave generously to everyone who came, and because of that sacrifice, he shines in Indra's hall. Then the second answer. Narada had seen Pandu in Yama's hall, and Pandu had seen Harishchandra's place. So Pandu gave Narada a message. Tell my son: you are able to conquer the earth, and your brothers obey you. Perform the Rajasuya. Then I, and our ancestors, may go to Indra's world. Sit with that. Yudhishthira's father died when the brothers were young, back in the forest, and has been gone this whole long serial. Now, in the brand-new hall, in front of everyone, a sage delivers his words. Not comfort. Not, I'm proud of you. A request, and a heavy one. There's something tender in it, though. Pandu is still thinking of his sons, and still thinking of his own fathers before him. A son is asked to do something so that his father can rise with his ancestors. And notice how it reaches him: not as a dream, not as a ghost, but through a guest in the sabha. The hall opened by feeding people is now where the dead can speak to the living. Tomorrow, Narada adds something far less welcome.
screen: `HARISHCHANDRA'S SACRIFICE.` · `PANDU SAW IT FROM YAMA'S HALL.` · `TELL MY SON: PERFORM THE RAJASUYA.` · `A FATHER, A SON, THE ANCESTORS.` · then, large: `THE DEAD SPEAK IN THE SABHA.`

segments.voice: Go gently with this one. Bring to mind a parent, grandparent or elder, living or gone, and something they hoped for you, large or small, spoken or never quite said. You don't need to agree with it or act on it; just let it be heard, the way Yudhishthira hears his father's words, and if you pray, hold that person in mind as you breathe.
Sabha. A hall, and its assembly. Today, in Yudhishthira's sabha, a sage carries a message from his father among the dead.
Your line: tell my son. A father's hope still reached him, through a guest. Day seven hundred fifty.

howItsDone: Hindu families honor their ancestors in shraddha rites, with offerings of food and water, and in the season of Pitru Paksha, when the ancestors are remembered together.

chat.says: What message did Pandu send his son through Narada?
options: Perform the Rajasuya, so Pandu and the ancestors may go to Indra's world.
Forgive your cousins, and give back the half kingdom you were given.
Leave the new hall and live simply in the forest, as I once did.
chat.meaning: Pandu, seen in Yama's hall, said through Narada: you can conquer the earth; perform the Rajasuya, so I and our ancestors may reach Indra's world.

Harishchandra.meaning: a king who shines in Indra's hall for his sacrifice

Rajasuya.meaning: the great royal sacrifice of a king over kings

Pandu.meaning: Yudhishthira's father, who died in the forest

Yama.meaning: lord of the dead, in whose hall Narada saw Pandu

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Lokapala Sabhakhyana Parva (Yudhishthira asks about Harishchandra and Pandu; Narada delivers Pandu's message)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm that Narada names Harishchandra as the human king in Indra's hall and attributes his place to the Rajasuya and his generosity.

'Died when the brothers were young, back in the forest' refers to Adi Parva; confirm phrasing.
